title: Incident acknowledgement card with annotated SLO delta and snapshot attachments
creator: Amrita Singh
description:
Design and prototype a compact Incident Acknowledgement Card that sits inline in the incident timeline and surfaces: a computed SLO delta (numeric + micro-sparkline), contextual summary, quick snapshot attachments (screenshots or logs excerpts), and one-click links to create or attach a postmortem. The intent is to reduce friction during acknowledgement: on-call engineers can see immediate SLO impact, attach visual evidence, use a templated acknowledgement message, and create a follow-up task without leaving the timeline. This ticket covers UX flows, visual design, accessibility, interaction states, and handoff notes for frontend and backend implementation.

Key behaviors: the card appears as a prominent compact row for any alert that is acknowledged; it shows the current SLO(s) affected and the delta from baseline (e.g., +0.7% error rate). If SLO data is not available, the card shows an informational fallback and a link to request SLO recalculation. Attachments can be dragged or pasted; each snapshot gets a small thumbnail and timestamp. The card also exposes a dropdown to select a predefined ack message, a free-text field, and a toggle to auto-create a follow-up task (prefilled title with actionable tags). The card should have lightweight animations and keyboard-first controls (focusable, enter to submit, esc to cancel).
acceptance_criteria: Ack card renders inline in incident timeline for any acknowledged alert
SLO delta displays a numeric value and a 6-point sparkline representing the immediate pre/post window
Attachment flow supports paste, drag-and-drop, and file select; thumbnail + timestamp shows immediately
One-click 'Attach to postmortem' links create or attach an existing postmortem (backend PR: ENG-6178) or surface a chooser if multiple PM docs exist
Templated ack messages available via dropdown and editable before send
'Create follow-up' toggle creates a task prefilled with alert, assignee, and priority metadata (integration with Linear/ENG APIs)
Keyboard accessibility: all actionable elements reachable and operable with keyboard-only navigation
QA E2E tests validate ack + attachment + follow-up creation in staging environment
design_notes: Prefer compact density: aim for a single-row primary display with an expandable details view for long messages and multiple attachments
SLO delta uses color semantics: red for worsening, green for improvement, neutral gray for no change. Use status icons (↑ ↓ —) for clarity but ensure color is not the sole indicator
Sparklines are 6 points representing the 30s/1m sampling window depending on the incident length; fallback to '—' when samples are missing
Attachment thumbnails are small (48px) with hover preview; limit visible thumbnails to 4 with a +N counter
tradeoffs: Inline card reduces context switching but increases timeline density; we mitigate with a collapsed state and focus-driven expansion
Real-time SLO computation is expensive; initial implementation will use cached SLO snapshots (ENG-6130) and show live recalculation status
Attachments stored temporarily in staging S3 namespace before commit to official artifact store to avoid blocking acknowledgment latency
accessibility_considerations: Ensure color contrast for numeric delta meets AA standard; provide textual delta for screen readers
Provide aria-live region updates for ack confirmation and attachment uploads
All interactive elements must have visible focus states and keyboard shortcuts (A = acknowledge, F = create follow-up)
Attachments must include alt text prompt on upload for image descriptions
qa_and_rollout_plan: Design sign-off -> small frontend spike -> backend SLO snapshot endpoint (ENG-6130) -> integration tests
Rollout behind 'incident-ack-card' feature flag, gradually enable for 10% of orgs then 50% after telemetry checks
Collect metrics: ack time delta (before vs after), follow-up creation rate, attachment upload success rate, error rates for SLO lookups
Post-release: survey on-call engineers in affected orgs and schedule 1:1 interviews for qualitative feedback
